([[Glendale, Wisconsin]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 20 | draft_team = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–present | team1 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Star]] ({{nasg|2026}}) * [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Third Team]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) | nbanew = 1630552 }} '''Jalen Tyrese Johnson''' (born December 18, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), with whom he has been selected to one All-Star game to date. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Johnson was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[Forward (basketball position)|forwards]] in the 2020 class. He finished his high school career at [[Nicolet High School]] in [[Glendale, Wisconsin]]. ==High school career== Johnson played his first two years of high school basketball for [[Sun Prairie High School]] in [[Sun Prairie, Wisconsin]]. He played under former head coach Jeff Boos, who was inducted into the Wisconsin Basketball Coaches Association (WBCA) Hall of Fame in 2020. As a freshman in 2016–17, Johnson averaged 15.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals, and 1.1 blocks to help his team to a 20–4 record. They were upset in the Regional Finals by [[Madison East High School]]. As a sophomore in 2017–18, Johnson averaged 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.9 steals, and 1.5 blocks to help his team to a 25–2 record. He led the Cardinals to their first state tournament Division 1 semifinals appearance. After his sophomore year he transferred to [[Nicolet High School]] in [[Glendale, Wisconsin]]. Johnson helped lead Nicolet to the Division 2 State Championship. He was named the Associated Press Player of the Year for Wisconsin.{{cite news |last=Masson |first=Jon |title=Jalen Johnson gains eligibility to play at Glendale Nicolet |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/jalen-johnson-gains-eligibility-to-play-at-glendale-nicolet/article_941c3303-4f41-5cdf-97df-9bbe00331c18.html |accessdate=March 29, 2020 |work=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |date=February 8, 2020 |language=en}} In 2019, Johnson transferred to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] for his senior year.{{cite web |last=Watson |first=John |date=August 5, 2019 |title=Duke's Jalen Johnson will transfer to IMG for senior season |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/Duke-commitment-jalen-johnson-will-team-up-with-top-duke-target-mark-williams-at-img-academy-in-florida-this-year-134218503/ |access-date=August 5, 2019 |website=[[247Sports]]}} On January 5, 2020, he left IMG Academy, before returning to Nicolet, though not necessarily to play basketball.{{cite web |last=Stewart |first=Mark |title=Duke recruit Jalen Johnson will return to Nicolet for school, not necessarily for basketball |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2020/01/17/jalen-johnson-return-nicolet-school-not-necessarily-hoops/4505762002/ |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 23, 2020 |date=January 17, 2020}} He was ruled eligible on February 8 to play the remainder of the season for Nicolet after never playing in a game for IMG. As a senior, Johnson averaged 24.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 9 games. He was selected to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=September 11, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Johnson was rated as a five-star recruit and the No.13 overall recruit in the 2020 high school class.{{Cite play [[college basketball]] at [[Duke University]] over offers from Arizona, Kentucky, and Wisconsin.{{cite web|title=Five-Star Small Forward Jalen Johnson Commits to Duke's 2020 bball = yes }} ==College career== The [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2020–21 Duke Blue Devils team]] entered the season in the top 10, and Johnson was its most highly rated player. In his first game, Johnson had 19 points and 19 rebounds against [[2020–21 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team|Coppin State]].{{cite news |title=Johnson, Steward help No. 9 Duke beat Coppin State 81-71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401259835 |access-date=November 28, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 28, 2020}} On November 30, 2020, Johnson earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Freshman of the Week honors.{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/11/30/athlete-awards-aluma-johnson-pick-up-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Aluma, Johnson Pick Up ACC Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=November 30, 2020}} On January 26, 2021, he scored 18 points and 6 rebounds in a 75–68 win over [[2020–21 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401265078|title=Duke snaps 3-game skid, holds off Georgia Tech for 75–68 win|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=January 27, 2021}} On February 15, 2021, Johnson announced that he would forgo the remainder of Duke's season to prepare for the [[2021 NBA draft]]. Leaving in the midst of a college season raised many questions, with Johnson claiming that the decision was in the best interest of his family and himself.{{Cite web |last=Beard |first=Aaron |date=February 15, 2021 |title=Duke’s Johnson is forgoing season, declaring for NBA draft |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/college/dukes-johnson-is-foregoing-season-declaring-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=February 16, 2021 |publisher=seattletimes.com}} During his 13 games as a Blue Devil, Johnson averaged 11.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2021/04/duke-mens-basketball-player-review-jalen-johnson|title=Duke men's basketball 2020–21 season review: Jalen Johnson|last=Gim|first=Eric|date=April 1, 2021|publisher=[[Duke Chronicle]]|access-date=July 29, 2021}} Duke ended its season with 13 wins and 11 losses. They finished 10th in the ACC with a 9–9 record. ==Professional career== === Atlanta Hawks (2021–present) === ==== Early years (2021–2024) ==== On July 29, 2021, Johnson was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 20th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Jack|last=Baer|title=Duke freshman Jalen Johnson picked 20th by Hawks after opting out of season|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-draft-duke-freshman-jalen-johnson-hawks-opt-out-season-024156771.html|website=sports.Yahoo.com|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}} On August 4, he signed with the Hawks.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Hawks Sign Jalen Johnson To Rookie Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/hawks-sign-jalen-johnson-to-rookie-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} Johnson appeared in 22 games during his rookie season with the Hawks in 2021–22, seeing limited minutes while splitting time between the NBA roster and the team’s [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]]. After the season ended, he underwent a non-surgical left knee procedure.{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2022 |title=ATLANTA HAWKS INJURY UPDATE – BOGDANOVIC, JOHNSON |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-injury-update-bogdanovic-johnson |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In the 2022–23 season, Johnson earned a more regular role off the bench for Atlanta, averaging 5.6 points and 4.0 rebounds in 70 games as he gradually expanded his playing time and contributions. Johnson’s 2023–24 season marked his first year as a primary starter, where he posted significant improvements across the board, setting then-career highs with averages of 16.0 points, 8.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game while starting 52 of 56 games. On April 4, 2024, He recorded his first career triple‑double, finishing with 28 points, 14 rebounds, and 11 assists in the Hawks’ 121–113 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |title=Hawks' Jalen Johnson: First career triple‑double |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-jalen-johnson-first-career-triple-double/ |website=CBS Sports |publisher=Paramount |date=April 4, 2024 |access-date=April 4, 2024}} ==== Breakthrough and injury (2024–2025) ==== On October 21, 2024, Johnson and the Hawks agreed to a five–year, $150 million contract extension.{{Cite web|title=Hawks, Jalen Johnson agree to 5-year, $150M extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41930446/hawks-jalen-johnson-agree-5-year-150m-extension|access-date=October 22, 2024|website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web|title=Forward Jalen Johnson signs multi-year extension with Hawks|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-jalen-johnson-extension|access-date=October 22, 2024|website=NBA.com|language=en}} In his fourth season, Johnson emerged as a breakout player for the Hawks, earning a starting role and averaging career highs of 18.9 points, 10.0 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game, along with 1.6 steals and 1.0 blocks in 36 games, before his season was cut short on January 29, 2025, due to shoulder surgery.{{Cite web|title=Reports: Hawks' Jalen Johnson (shoulder) out for season|url=https://www.nba.com/news/atlanta-hawks-jalen-johnson-shoulder-out-for-season|date=January 29, 2025|website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=January 29, 2025 |title=Hawks' Johnson to have season-ending surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43611422/sources-hawks-jalen-johnson-season-ending-surgery |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} At that point of the season, Johnson was one of the leading candidates for the [[NBA Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]] award.{{cite web |last=Lakhani |first=Iliyan |title=Jalen Johnson has already taken home the MIP in our hearts |url=https://www.peachtreehoops.com/2025/1/20/24345663/jalen-johnson-atlanta-hawks-most-improved-award-opinion |website=Peachtree Hoops |publisher=SB Nation |date=January 20, 2025 |access-date=January 20, 2025}} ==== First All-Star and All-NBA appearances (2025–present) ==== On November 13, 2025, Johnson recorded 31 points, 18 rebounds, 14 assists, seven steals and four three-pointers in a 132–122 win over the [[Utah Jazz]]. The performance marked the third [[triple-double]] of his career and his first of the season, and he set a then career high in points, alongside new career highs in rebounds, assists, and steals while matching his career high in made three-pointers. With the performance, Johnson also became the first player in NBA history to record 31 points, 18 rebounds, 14 assists, and seven steals in a single game.{{cite web |title=Jalen Johnson & Onyeka Okongwu’s Historic Games Power Hawks Win Over Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/jalen-johnson-onyeka-okongwus-historic-games-power-hawks-win-over-jazz |website=NBA.com |date=November 13, 2025| access-date=November 13, 2025}} On November 28, Johnson put up his fourth career triple-double with 29 points, 12 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 130–123 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-jalen-johnson-shines-win-cavs|title=Hawks’ Jalen Johnson shines in statement win over Cavs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Imran|first=Abdullah|date=November 28, 2025|access-date=November 28, 2025}}{{cite 2025|access-date=November 28, 2025}} On November 30, Johnson notched a then career-high 41 points, along with 14 rebounds and seven assists in a 142–134 double overtime victory against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite AV media|title={{!}} Atlanta Hawks|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/videos/jalen-johnson-scores-career-high-41-pts-in-hawks-double-ot-win-in-philadelphia|language=en|access-date=2025-12-01|via=www.nba.com}}{{Cite web|title=40-point special: Jalen Johnson leads Hawks to double OT win over 76ers|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/2025/12/40-point-special-hawks-jalen-johnson-leads-team-to-2ot-win-over-76ers/|website=ajc|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}} On December 5, Johnson recorded the fastest triple-double in Hawks franchise history and the second-fastest in NBA history against the [[Denver Nuggets]] by achieving 11 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in the first half and ending with 21 points, 18 rebounds, and 16 assists in a 134–133 loss.{{Cite news |last=Hollinger |first=John |author-link=John Hollinger |date=2025-12-06 |title=Hawks’ Jalen Johnson posts second-fastest triple-double in NBA history |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6866847/2025/12/05/jalen-johnson-triple-double-hawks-first-half/ |access-date=2025-12-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-jalen-johnson-makes-atlanta-history-1st-half-triple-double-nuggets|title= Jalen Johnson makes Hawks history with 1st half triple-double vs. Nuggets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=December 6, 2025|access-date=December 6, 2025}} On December 18, Johnson scored a career-high 43 points, nearly posting a triple-double with 11 rebounds and 9 assists in a 133–126 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |title= Starting 5: Recapping a busy Thursday night |url= https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-dec-19-2025 |website=NBA.com |date=December 18, 2025| access-date=December 19, 2025}} On January 31, 2026, Johnson put up a triple-double with 33 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 129–124 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. It was his eighth triple-double of the season, setting the record for the most triple-doubles in a single season in Hawks franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-jalen-johnson-sets-new-franchise-record-loss-pacers|title=Jalen Johnson sets new franchise record in Hawks’ loss to Pacers|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=January 31, 2026|access-date=January 31, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.oskaloosa.com/sports/national_sports/pacers-beat-hawks-129-124-overcoming-jalen-johnsons-triple-double/article_e59d4873-3895-5f5d-8dea-c1046ac1868d.html|title=Pacers beat Hawks 129-124, overcoming Jalen Johnson's triple-double|website=The Oskaloosa Herald|date=January 31, 2026|access-date=January 31, 2026}} On February 1, Johnson was named to his first [[2026 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as a Eastern Conference reserve.{{Cite web |title=2026 NBA All-Star reserves announced on NBC/Peacock |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-all-star-reserves |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} Johnson finished the regular season with 13 triple-doubles, joining [[Bob Pettit]] in Hawks franchise history with multiple 30-point, 15-rebound, and 8-assist games.{{Cite web |title=Jalen Johnson Triple Doubles This Season Game Logs |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/jalen-johnson-triple-doubles-this-season-game-logs |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=StatMuse |language=en}} The Hawks finished with a 46–36 record and the sixth seed, and Johnson was named to the [[All-NBA]] Third Team, earning the first All-NBA selection of his career.{{cite web |title=2025–26 Kia All-NBA Teams announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-nba-teams-announced |website=NBA.com |date=2026-05-24 |access-date=2026-05-27}} The Hawks faced the [[New York Knicks]] during their first-round playoff series. On April 18, Johnson put up 23 points, seven rebounds, and three assists in a 113–102 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title=BRUNSON AND TOWNS LEAD THE KNICKS PAST THE HAWKS 113-102 IN GAME 1 OF THEIR SERIES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500121 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On April 23, he recorded 24 points, ten rebounds, eight assists, and two steals in a 109–108 Game 3 win, which gave the Hawks a 2–1 series lead.{{Cite web |title=MCCOLLUM RUINS KNICKS' NIGHT AGAIN, LEADING THE HAWKS TO A 109-108 VICTORY AND A 2-1 LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500123 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} They eventually lost to the Knicks in six games. ==Personal life== Johnson is the son of Stacy and Roderick Johnson. He has three brothers. His father played college basketball at [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] and [[Southeast Missouri State University]] before playing professionally for two years in Poland. His mother also played college basketball at [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]]. His brother Rod, played basketball at [[University of Tennessee at Chattanooga]] and his younger brother [[Kobe Johnson|Kobe]] played basketball at [[University of Southern California]] and [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]].{{cite web |title=Jalen Johnson - 2020-21 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jalen-johnson/16343 |website=Duke
